key_insight: Learning to predict actions may weaken a world model’s ability to generate video that matches language instructions. SWAM investigates how data and supervision design can preserve this cross-modal alignment; the supplied abstract is incomplete and does not establish specific results.
problem_solved: World action models jointly predict video and actions from language, but existing approaches offer limited guidance on maintaining language–video alignment when action learning is introduced.
method: Study language-conditioned world action models that jointly predict video and actions.
Investigate how action learning affects language–video alignment inherited from video pretraining.
Examine data and supervision design for preserving alignment; dataset details and specific techniques are missing from the supplied abstract.
impact: This work highlights alignment preservation as a key consideration when extending video models with action prediction. It may inform training-data and supervision choices, though practical benefits cannot be verified from the excerpt.

paper_title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
